transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-20 15:30 UTC | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Luca (Product), Tomah (Solutions) — Aisha (CTO Verdigris), Ben (Head of Cloud), Marta (Integration Lead), Colin (Security)

Summary: kickoff to converge on packaging and ops for Verdigris connector and marketplace listing. Heavy focus on Helm/operator, KMS integrations, and initial perf benchmark.

[00:00] Evan Morales: Alright, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Evan, AE on the partner team at Redwood...uh, do quick round robin?
[00:18] Aisha Karim: Hey all, Aisha — CTO at Verdigris. We're leading the hybrid connector project, want to get this listed in the marketplace and also support on-prem customers.
[00:26] Ben Yamada: Ben, head of cloud infra, I'll be hands-on with their kube clusters and networking.
[00:34] Priya Singh: Priya, Redwood SE — I'll own the integration for the connector and benchmark plan.
[00:38] Marta Alvarez: Marta here, integration lead, will actually run the helm charts and validate installation.
[00:44] Evan Morales: Great. Luca from product and Tomah from solutions will chime in for packaging details.

[01:05] Luca Rossi: High level agenda: packing checklist for marketplace, operator vs plain helm, KMS compatibility, air-gap/air-gapped notes, quantization for smaller models, and acceptance criteria for the pilot.
[01:18] Marta Alvarez: Quick note — some of our regs require us to use customer-managed KMS and an HSM, so we need to be sure Redwood's private plane can talk to our KMS, or the connector can be configured to use it locally.
[01:32] Colin Park: and audit logs, right, we need to capture token-level traces for compliance, not full content but metadata — timestamps, model id, route, request ID.

[02:05] Priya Singh: Totally. On Redwood Private we support KMS integration via customer-managed keys; there's also an HSM option for on-prem. We'll share the integration doc but caveat: some of the fields in the audit log are configurable and some are redacted by default.
[02:22] Aisha Karim: When you say "share the doc" is that public or will you add a non-disclosure for the HSM keys walkthrough?
[02:30] Tomah Li: We'll share a gating doc — we can do an NDA addendum if needed, but typically the HSM runbook is in the private repo access for partner integrators with a signed doc.

[03:00] Ben Yamada: Networking — our ops team runs isolated clusters in a VPC with strict egress. Does the connector require outbound to Redwood endpoints during runtime or only at control plane time?
[03:15] Priya Singh: Good question. For the marketplace operator case, the connector can be configured in two modes: "managed-control-plane" where it talks back to Redwood for updates, or "air-gapped" mode where we bundle model artifacts and the control plane is local. Runtime inference can stay fully on-prem if configured. Some features like usage telemetry require egress unless you opt-in to offline metering.
[03:41] Marta Alvarez: So for our use-case we need local inference with only periodic telemetry uploads — we can accept batched upload via an ops-only window.
[03:52] Priya Singh: Yes, batching and local metering is supported — note that for billing reconciliation the marketplace listing expects metering hooks. We'll share the marketplace metering API and a sample uploader.

[04:20] Evan Morales: On packaging — Luca, operator vs plain helm — pros/cons quick?
[04:28] Luca Rossi: Operator gives lifecycle hooks, CRDs for routing policies, easier upgrades and can wire into model rollout automation. Helm chart is lighter weight for customers not wanting an operator. For a marketplace listing we recommend operator for enterprise customers, but provide a helm-only minimal package for quick installs.
[04:50] Marta Alvarez: We prefer helm-only for the pilot to reduce blast radius, then operator for GA.

[05:10] Priya Singh: Noted. We'll produce both artifacts with the operator in a separate chart. We'll include a sample values.yaml for a private deployment pattern with KMS endpoint and local model storage.

[06:02] Ben Yamada: Quantization — some of our teams will want int8 to reduce memory footprint. How does Redwood handle multiple model variants and auto-routing?
[06:18] Priya Singh: Redwood runtime supports serving multiple quantized variants and smart routing by policy — latency vs cost. For edge cases we can route to the lower quantized model when under capacity constraints. There is a small perf delta on some LLMs where quantization introduces hallucination risk; we recommend running evals on your prompt sets.
[06:45] Marta Alvarez: Do you have an eval harness we can use?
[06:48] Priya Singh: Yes — we'll include an evaluation harness and a baseline prompt set. We can also help with a regression alert if quality drops post-quantization.

[07:30] Aisha Karim: About the marketplace listing metadata — SLA terms, logos, packaging, pricing tiers — what's required to go live?
[07:40] Evan Morales: There's a checklist: listing assets, security review (SOC2/ISO), pricing metadata, billing hooks, support contacts, and an on-boarding test that validates the helm chart. We'll send the checklist.
[07:54] Luca Rossi: Also, we need a compatibility matrix for supported Kubernetes versions, and a note about supported GPUs/quantization profiles.

[08:20] Ben Yamada: On the GPU side, some of our customers use T4s, others A10Gs — we need to know expected memory and sequence length tradeoffs.
[08:30] Priya Singh: We'll include recommended resource profiles per model variant and sequence length assumptions used in our benchmarks. For quantized int8, memory is lower but be careful with context window > 2k, can run into perf cliffs.

[09:05] Marta Alvarez: For air-gapped installs, how are model blobs coming in? We may have to transfer via secure artifact bundle.
[09:12] Tomah Li: We support a model artifact tarball with signature verification and a CLI tool to load model into local object storage. That's what most partners use for air-gapped onboarding.

[09:40] Colin Park: Security — we need to ensure private keys never leave our HSM. The connector should be able to call the KMS via a local endpoint and not expose keys.
[09:50] Priya Singh: Correct. The connector can be configured to use customer KMS endpoints. We do not persist raw keys; only key identifiers and credentials per customer's KMS integration pattern. We'll share a sample KMS config with RBAC notes.

[10:25] Aisha Karim: Logging detail: Colin asked about token-level metadata only. We need minimal PII. How do you handle redaction?
[10:33] Priya Singh: We have redaction toggles. Default is metadata-only; full payload logging is off by default. We'll provide the config that controls at token level and whether to keep prefix caching keys — note that some caching telemetry emits hash pointers which you can turn off.

[11:00] Evan Morales: Pilot/benchmark plan — Priya, walk through proposed scope.
[11:07] Priya Singh: Plan: a 2-phase pilot. Phase 1: install helm chart on Verdigris staging cluster, verify install and connectivity (control plane + local inference mode). Phase 2: run perf benchmark with synthetic traces and 3 representative prompt families (short chat, long context 6k tokens, embedding workloads). We'll run traces at 10-20 RPS to validate latency p95 and throughput. Acceptance criteria: p95 latency under X ms for short chat (we'll define exact), stable KV cache hit rate > 60% for repeated prefixes, and no errors > 0.1%.
[11:47] Marta Alvarez: Do you have a script for generating long traces?
[11:50] Priya Singh: Yes — that's the script we'll share, plus an example workload file and a collector to upload results.

[12:20] Ben Yamada: Billing hooks — how do we reconcile usage if telemetry is batched?
[12:29] Evan Morales: The metering hook accepts batched usage files with signed timestamps. The marketplace expects periodic metering files; we can also do reconciliation if there is a mismatch within a threshold.

[12:55] Aisha Karim: Any gotchas to watch during the helm install for environments with strict PSPs?
[13:02] Tomah Li: We'll provide a PSP-compatible manifest and instructions for PSP/OPA gates. Also a note about init containers that require additional capabilities; we try to avoid privileged containers for default.

[13:30] Priya Singh: On model routing and fallback — can we agree on a policy? If a request to quantized model fails quality eval during pilot, fall back to non-quantized variant for that API route. We'll test the automatic fallback logic.
[13:48] Marta Alvarez: Yes please. We don't want customer-facing regressions.

[14:10] Aisha Karim: For the marketplace listing, what's Redwood's review timeline?
[14:16] Evan Morales: Once we submit the packaging and security artifacts it usually takes 7-10 business days for listing review, but HSM and custom KMS may take longer due to manual checks. So plan for 2-3 weeks for first listing if all materials are provided.

[15:00] Ben Yamada: Competitors — they asked about similar connectors from CloudWave; how do you differ?
[15:06] Luca Rossi: We focus on production economics — smarter batching, prefix/KV caching, and model variant routing baked into the runtime plus strong dev experience for rollouts. Also tighter ops integrations for marketplace listings.

[16:02] Marta Alvarez: Quick demo request — can we get a short install demo in a follow-up?
[16:07] Evan Morales: Yes, we'll schedule a 45 minute install walkthrough with a live helm install in Verdigris staging. Suggest next week or the week after depending on staging availability.

[16:40] Priya Singh: I'll follow up with links: helm chart repo, sample values.yaml, metering API spec, and the eval harness.

[17:05] Aisha Karim: On legal/compliance, we'll need Redwood's SOC2 and the partner carve-out for the marketplace listing — Colin will coordinate.

[18:00] Colin Park: I'll add my list of required audit fields and send it to Evan and Tomah.

[18:22] Evan Morales: Recap of next steps: Redwood shares packaging checklist and artifacts (Helm + operator examples), benchmark script, metering API. Verdigris provides staging access, SOC2 artifacts, and runs the pilot.

[18:45] Marta Alvarez: Sounds good. One last question — what about model weights distribution for air-gapped customers, is there an S3-style signed artifact flow?
[18:55] Tomah Li: Yes, we provide signed tarballs with SHA256 and a signature, plus a CLI that verifies signature before importing. We'll include the signing workflow doc.

[19:20] Ben Yamada: Perfect. We'll aim to have staging access ready by March 4th.
[19:30] Evan Morales: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with an email capturing these notes and action items.

[62:00] Meeting end / recording stopped.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps around "KV cache" -> "K V see" and "operator" sometimes transcribed as "op-erator" in the export. Natural speech, some overlaps and short crosstalk.
